The right hand side of the dilemma might not look too bad at first. We might think, for example, that we can explain God’s creation of contingent things in terms of God’s deciding to create contingent things.

But the problem is that the existence of the infinite series is itself contingent. So, as in the case of the geometry books, we can ask: what explains why there is such a series at all? And if the principle of sufficient reason is true, this question must have an answer.
